papers.title: A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a major determinant of poor prognosis in systemic lupus erythematosus, yet reliable tools for early identification of unfavorable renal outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to identify early prognostic factors for complete renal response (CRR) at 12 months in active LN and to develop interpretable machine learning (ML) models for early prediction of treatment response. In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML mode
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 400 active lupus nephritis patients used machine learning to predict complete renal response at 12 months, drawing on predictors measured at baseline and at the 3-month treatment milestone. The work identifies early prognostic factors and develops interpretable ML models for early identification of patients likely to have unfavorable renal outcomes.

papers.title: Comparing longitudinal regression and deep-learning models for healthcare utilisation prediction: evidence from the SHARE longitudinal panel in Europe.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of outpatient utilisation is essential for health-policy planning, yet work has focused on classical models or deep learning in claims/electronic health record settings. Using longitudinal micro-data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe—10 777 adults observed in Waves 5, 6, 8 and 9 (2013, 2015, 2019–2020 and 2021–2022)—we compare classical longitudinal models with sequence-aware neural networks for forecasting Wave 9 outpatient visits from unevenly spaced histories.
papers.summary: This study compares classical longitudinal regression models with sequence-aware deep-learning networks for predicting outpatient healthcare utilisation using data from 10,777 older adults in the SHARE panel across four unevenly spaced waves. It provides a head-to-head benchmark of traditional statistical versus neural approaches in a survey-based (non-EHR) setting, addressing the challenge of irregular observation intervals. The findings offer guidance on model choice for health-policy forecasting from longitudinal panel data.

papers.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts.
papers.abstract: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the r
papers.summary: This study combines whole-cell phage display, next-generation sequencing, machine learning, and flow cytometry to identify short peptide ligands that bind lung cancer cells with specific KRAS mutations (wild-type, G12C, G12D, G12V). The authors train a multimodal probabilistic model on the selection outputs to interpret complex biopanning data and nominate candidate targeting peptides. The approach demonstrates how ML can help deconvolute phage display selections for genotype-defined cancer contexts.

papers.title: Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory diseases consist of a diverse group of conditions characterized by immune responses leading to inflammation causing damage and abnormality in function. Atopic dermatitis (AD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) both exhibit aberrant Th2 cell activity, leading to epithelial barrier dysfunction in the skin and gut, respectively. Although both diseases share similar features, differences in their tissue-specific pathology, clinical manifestations, and immune profiles may provide valuable insights into the distinct mechanisms underlying each disease.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning to analyze blood plasma protein profiles from patients with atopic dermatitis and ulcerative colitis, two inflammatory diseases that share Th2-driven immune activity but affect different tissues. The analysis identified protein biomarkers that can distinguish between the two conditions, offering insight into their distinct disease mechanisms. These findings may support more precise diagnosis and understanding of tissue-specific inflammation.

papers.title: A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.
papers.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with substantial global mortality. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have shown promise for mortality prediction, evidence focused specifically on critically ill patients remains limited. In addition, meaningful clinical implementation requires models that rely on a minimal set of readily available variables to enable rapid risk stratification. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based model for predicting mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with an emphasis
papers.summary: This multicenter registry study develops a deep learning model to predict mortality among critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU, using a deliberately minimal set of readily available clinical variables to support rapid risk stratification. The work addresses a gap in AI-based mortality prediction specifically for the ICU population and emphasizes practical clinical deployability.

papers.title: MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) supports precision medicine in cancer care, but accurate assessment of missense variant pathogenicity, especially for variants without established consensus, remains challenging. Various computational tools have been developed for variant functional prediction, but most current tools rely solely on variant-level features and do not capture the clinical context of individual patients. To address this limitation, we developed MARiO (Missense Alteration Risk identifier in Oncology), a machine-learning model that integrates variant-level features and patient-l
papers.summary: MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of tools that assess variants in isolation. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation for comprehensive genomic profiling in precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus. The approach represents a step toward context-aware variant classification in clinical cancer genomics.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Analysis of Peripheral Blood Smear for Prediction of Acute Inflammatory States and Chronic Comorbidities: Development and Internal Validation Study.
papers.abstract: Peripheral blood smear (PBS) examination provides morphological information on immune cells that reflects systemic pathophysiology, yet whether it can be used to predict systemic states has not been systematically established.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether deep learning applied to peripheral blood smear images can predict systemic conditions such as acute inflammation and chronic comorbidities. The authors develop and internally validate a model, suggesting that morphological features of immune cells captured on smears carry predictive signal beyond traditional clinical use. The work is a development and internal validation study, so external validation is still needed.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.
papers.abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors pro
papers.summary: This study presents a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight human basal ganglia regions, revealing cell-type- and region-specific regulatory landscapes and gene regulatory networks. The authors identify combinatorial homeobox transcription factor expression as a key driver of cell identity in this brain region. This resource provides a foundation for understanding basal ganglia function and dysfunction in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) i
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk multi-omics data to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying C16orf74 as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The authors show that C16orf74 expression is associated with EMT-associated malignant states and has prognostic relevance in HNSCC patients.

papers.title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.
papers.abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning-based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog-aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence-based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning-based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize
papers.summary: EZpred is a deep learning method that improves enzyme function prediction (EC number assignment) by incorporating features from unlabeled sequence homologs, analogous to how homolog-aware structure predictors like AlphaFold outperform single-sequence methods. Unlike prior models that only use function labels from homologs, EZpred leverages unlabeled homolog sequences to boost accuracy. This demonstrates that homolog-derived features are valuable for functional annotation, not just structure prediction.

papers.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
papers.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors combine AI-based single-cell imaging with morphology-guided label-free enrichment to isolate tumor cells from malignant effusions, which are typically dominated by immune cells. Genomic profiling of the enriched cells reveals phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity, relatedness, and divergence among metastatic tumor populations. This approach makes an underused clinical sample type more tractable for single-cell molecular characterization.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entering obstetrics and prenatal medicine, particularly in prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal magnetic resonance imaging, genomic screening, risk prediction and clinical decision support. The aim of this review was to summarize current evidence, recent developments and implementation requirements for AI-based applications in prenatal care.
papers.summary: This review surveys the current evidence for AI applications in obstetrics and prenatal medicine, covering prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal MRI, genomic screening, risk prediction, and clinical decision support. It emphasizes the state of clinical validation and the practical requirements for implementing these tools in prenatal care.

papers.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.
papers.abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid populati
papers.summary: The authors present a new method that combines graph theory and machine learning to identify SARS-CoV-2 lineages undergoing rapid population growth from large volumes of genetic sequence data. By representing distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians, they extract spectral features that flag emerging lineages for real-time epidemic monitoring. This offers a scalable way to prioritize sequences of concern amid massive genomic surveillance streams.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models Incorporating TGFBIp Expression for Prognosis Prediction in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for diverse prognostic tools. Transforming growth factor-β-induced protein (TGFBIp) has been implicated in ovarian cancer progression, but its incremental prognostic value within machine learning frameworks remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates machine learning models that incorporate TGFBIp expression to predict prognosis in epithelial ovarian cancer, addressing the need for better prognostic tools given the disease's clinical heterogeneity. The work tests whether adding TGFBIp expression improves prognostic prediction within ML frameworks, a question not previously explored.

papers.title: Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate clinical correlates of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults, compare seven classification models, and interpret the selected gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier. This single-center observational study included 572 adults reported to be aged ≥ 60 years who received care between June 2021 and June 2023, comprising 385 participants classified as having persistent AF and 187 comparators. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) were used for candidate-variable assessment and f
papers.summary: This single-center observational study of 572 older adults compared seven classification models for identifying persistent atrial fibrillation and selected a gradient boosting machine classifier as the best performer. The work also examined clinical correlates of persistent AF in this population and interpreted the chosen model's predictors. It is a narrow, single-center clinical modeling study with limited generalizability.

papers.title: Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Computational methods are increasingly applied to the discovery of plant-derived peptides, but the extent, composition and reporting practice of this literature have not been mapped. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed were searched for records published between 2021 and 2026. Of 5062 unique records, 593 were screened at title and abstract, 88 full texts were assessed, 80 sources met all five eligibility criteria and 79 were charted. Overall, 49 (62.0%) were primary studies, 12 (15.2%) described a tool or database and 18 (
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the literature (2021–2026) on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources. It finds that most work consists of primary studies, with a smaller share describing tools or databases, and highlights gaps in reporting practice across the field. The review provides a structured overview of methods, scope, and reporting standards in this emerging area.

papers.title: Macronutrient composition and incident hypertension during China's nutrition transition: a longitudinal cohort analysis of the China Health and Nutrition Survey.
papers.abstract: China's nutrition transition has shifted dietary macronutrient composition while hypertension prevalence has risen. Whether the routinely available macronutrient composition adequately captures the risk of incident hypertension remains unclear.
papers.summary: This longitudinal cohort analysis uses China Health and Nutrition Survey data to examine whether macronutrient composition (carbohydrate, fat, protein) predicts incident hypertension during China's nutrition transition. The study aims to determine if routinely collected dietary macronutrient data can adequately capture hypertension risk, addressing a gap in understanding how dietary shifts during rapid nutritional change relate to rising hypertension prevalence.

papers.title: Integrating large-scale serum baseline metabolomics and APOE ε4 genotype status for the non-invasive detection of Alzheimer's disease in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.
papers.abstract: Accurate Alzheimer's disease (AD) detection remains challenging and often requires invasive or costly procedures. Blood-based metabolomic signatures offer a promising non-invasive comparative approach for disease stratification. This study aimed to evaluate whether large-scale serum metabolite panel combined with apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 genotype status could distinguish AD from cognitively normal (CN) individuals within the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.
papers.summary: This study tested whether a large panel of serum metabolites, combined with APOE ε4 genotype status, could distinguish Alzheimer's disease patients from cognitively normal individuals in the ADNI cohort. The work evaluates a non-invasive, blood-based approach as an alternative to costly or invasive AD diagnostics. It reports on the comparative performance of metabolomic signatures for disease stratification.

papers.title: Machine learning for host-pathogen protein-protein interaction prediction: A tutorial paper.
papers.abstract: The study of Host-Pathogen Protein-Protein Interactions (HP-PPIs) is critical for understanding mechanisms of infectious disease and for the development of therapeutic interventions. Computational prediction of HP-PPIs has become essential due to the limitations of experimental approaches, which are labour-intensive and expensive. In this tutorial, we present a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for HP-PPI prediction implemented in Google Colab. The workflow consists of six stages implemented in six Google Colab notebooks: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, machin
papers.summary: This tutorial paper presents a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for predicting host-pathogen protein-protein interactions, implemented across six Google Colab notebooks covering dataset preparation, preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training. It aims to make computational HP-PPI prediction accessible to researchers without extensive computational infrastructure. The work is primarily educational rather than introducing new methodology.

papers.title: SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling.
papers.abstract: Accurate battery modeling is essential for reliable state estimation in modern applications, such as predicting the remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy in battery management systems. Existing approaches face several limitations: model-based methods require a large number of physical parameters; data-driven methods rely heavily on labeled datasets; and current physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often lack aging adaptation, still depend on many physical parameters, or require continuous state regeneration. In this work, we propose SeqBattNet, a discrete-state PINN with
papers.summary: SeqBattNet is a physics-informed neural network for battery modeling that uses a discrete-state formulation and incorporates aging adaptation, aiming to predict remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy for battery management systems. The approach is designed to reduce reliance on large labeled datasets and extensive physical parameter tuning while handling battery aging effects that existing PINNs often ignore. This is a battery-engineering modeling contribution rather than a biological or biomedical one.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota-immune-metabolism axis has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis; however, the key host molecular targets linking peripheral dysregulation to central neurodegeneration remain elusive.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics Mendelian randomization to test whether gut microbiota, immune, and metabolic traits causally influence Alzheimer's disease, and identifies DDX17 as a potential mediating host molecule on the gut-immune-metabolism axis. The work nominates a specific molecular link between peripheral dysregulation and central neurodegeneration, though the evidence is genetic-instrument based and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: Screening of oxidative stress-related signature genes and construction of an interpretable discriminant model for preeclampsia.
papers.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy complication threatening maternal and fetal health, and its onset and progression are closely associated with placental oxidative stress. However, a systematic understanding of oxidative stress-related genes in PE and their roles in immune regulation remains lacking.
papers.summary: This study screens for oxidative stress-related signature genes in preeclampsia and builds an interpretable discriminant model to distinguish PE from normal pregnancies. It also explores how these genes relate to immune regulation in the placenta, aiming to fill a gap in systematic understanding of oxidative stress biology in PE.

papers.title: A multisource clinical deep learning model for early identification of mental disorders in first-visit psychiatric patients.
papers.abstract: Mental disorders often present with overlapping symptoms at the first psychiatric visit, making early identification difficult. This study included 5802 first-visit psychiatric patients and developed a TUCH-FT for multi-label classification of mental disorders using demographic information, clinical history, and item-level Symptom Checklist-90 data. Final diagnostic labels were determined through longitudinal follow-up, treatment response, and psychiatric expert evaluation. The original FT-Transformer places heterogeneous clinical variables in a single sequence, which may weaken source-specifi
papers.summary: This study developed a deep learning model (TUCH-FT) to classify multiple mental disorders in 5,802 first-visit psychiatric patients using demographic, clinical history, and item-level SCL-90 symptom data, with final diagnoses confirmed through longitudinal follow-up and expert evaluation. The model modifies the FT-Transformer architecture to better handle heterogeneous clinical variables from different sources, aiming to support early identification when symptoms overlap. The work demonstrates a multisource deep learning approach for psychiatric diagnostic support at the first visit.

papers.title: An interpretable machine learning model using routine clinical indicators for early pediatric sepsis risk stratification: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide. The 2024 Phoenix Sepsis Criteria emphasize early recognition of organ dysfunction. Conventional diagnostics like blood cultures are time-consuming, and existing machine learning models lack early pathogen-level classification. A machine learning framework for early pediatric sepsis warning and Gram-stain pathogen classification was developed and validated using routine clinical indicators.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective study developed and validated an interpretable machine learning model that uses routine clinical indicators to stratify pediatric sepsis risk early and to classify Gram-stain pathogen type. The approach aims to support earlier recognition of organ dysfunction aligned with the 2024 Phoenix Sepsis Criteria, addressing the time delays of blood cultures and the lack of pathogen-level classification in prior models.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by complex pathophysiological processes including abnormal mechanical stress and immune microenvironment remodeling. Although mechanical stimulus is known to trigger maladaptive cardiac remodeling, the systematic role of mechanical stimulus-related genes (MSRGs) in HF diagnosis and immune modulation remains poorly defined. This study aims to identify MSRG-based diagnostic biomarkers, characterize molecular subtypes, and explore their cellular localization and immune microenvironment interactions in HF.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify mechanical stimulus-related genes as diagnostic biomarkers for heart failure and to characterize how these genes relate to immune microenvironment remodeling. It also defines molecular subtypes of heart failure and explores the cellular localization of these genes. The work suggests that mechanical stress-responsive gene signatures could aid diagnosis and reveal immune-related mechanisms in heart failure.

papers.title: Development of a Machine-Learning Model for Strongyloidiasis Risk Stratification in Migrant Populations.
papers.abstract: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection with the potential for fatal hyperinfection, underscoring the need for screening strategies. A machine-learning model was developed and externally validated to support strongyloidiasis risk stratification among migrants from endemic areas.
papers.journal: Research and reports in tropical medicine
papers.summary: This study developed and externally validated a machine-learning model to stratify migrants from endemic areas by their risk of strongyloidiasis, a parasitic infection that can cause fatal hyperinfection. The model aims to support targeted screening strategies in migrant populations, where universal screening may be impractical.

papers.title: A lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for Kazakh Sign Language recognition under signer-independent conditions.
papers.abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) in low-resource sign languages is still limited due to the lack of annotated data, high variability of signers, and lack of benchmarks; Kazakh Sign Language (KzSL) is a representative example of such a low-resource language. The proposed research introduces a novel method for isolated KzSL recognition based on a purpose-collected dataset of RGB video streams of five signers, represented by 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, facial, and hand landmark vectors extracted using MediaPipe Holistic. The final dataset consists of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 output c
papers.summary: The authors present a lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for recognizing isolated Kazakh Sign Language gestures from RGB video, using MediaPipe Holistic to extract 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, face, and hand landmark vectors. They built a purpose-collected dataset of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 classes from five signers and evaluate under signer-independent conditions, addressing the low-resource setting where annotated data and benchmarks are scarce. The work is a domain-specific application contribution rather than a general methodological advance.

papers.title: SelCysML: a hybrid ML-BLAST pipeline for the automated identification and functional annotation of bacterial selenoproteins.
papers.abstract: Selenoproteins are characterized by the incorporation of selenocysteine (Sec) via UGA codon recoding, play vital roles in redox homeostasis and enzymatic catalysis. Despite this biological significance, their computational identification remains challenging, and recent assessments confirm that public databases suffer from widespread annotation errors, often misclassifying these proteins. Current predictive tools frequently operate as "black boxes" with limited interpretability or lack integrated functional validation layers, which contributes to high false-positive rates and persistent ambigui
papers.summary: The authors present SelCysML, a hybrid pipeline that combines machine learning with BLAST-based homology search to automatically identify bacterial selenoproteins and annotate their functions. The tool addresses widespread misannotation in public databases by adding interpretable functional validation layers, aiming to reduce false positives that plague existing 'black box' predictors. It targets the difficult problem of detecting selenocysteine incorporation via UGA recoding, which standard gene-finding tools routinely miss.

papers.title: Dietary amino acid composition and elevated fasting glucose in children and adolescents from four Chinese provinces: a cross-sectional study combining regression and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Using an integrated analytical pipeline that combines regression and machine learning, with nonlinear dose-response modeling, this cross-sectional study sought to examine dietary amino acid composition in relation to elevated fasting glucose (EFG) in children and adolescents.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of children and adolescents from four Chinese provinces examines whether the amino acid composition of the diet is associated with elevated fasting glucose. The authors combine regression analysis with machine learning and nonlinear dose-response modeling to identify dietary amino acid patterns linked to elevated fasting glucose. The work suggests that specific dietary amino acid profiles may be relevant to early glucose dysregulation in youth.

papers.title: A reproducible open-data framework for interpretable breast cancer diagnosis and cytopathology education.
papers.abstract: Quantitative nuclear morphology links cytopathological assessment with interpretable diagnostic modeling and provides a practical foundation for teaching medical artificial intelligence. This study evaluated a reproducible framework that connects nuclear feature interpretation, malignant-versus-benign classification, and evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.
papers.summary: This study presents a reproducible open-data framework that uses quantitative nuclear morphology features to classify breast cytopathology samples as malignant or benign while keeping the diagnostic reasoning interpretable. The framework also serves as a teaching tool for medical AI, linking feature-level interpretation to evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.
